zotero.abstractNote: Deep learning models for medical image analysis have shown impressive performance, but their deployment in clinical settings is hindered by concerns regarding fairness and interpretability. While predictive fairness metrics ensure that model performance is equitable across demographic groups, they do not guarantee that the model relies on the same clinical features for all patients. In this work, we propose a framework to quantify attribution consistency across demographic groups in the context of diabetic retinopathy screening. We evaluate the consistency of saliency maps generated by different attribution methods and demonstrate that models can exhibit high predictive fairness while maintaining significant disparities in attribution consistency. Our results highlight the importance of evaluating both predictive and attributional fairness to ensure the reliability and trustworthiness of AI-based diagnostic tools.
